stem: Two circles M and N have radius lengths ${=r1}$ cm and ${=r2}$ cm. They are intersecting, and the length of MN is a whole number of centimetres. How many different values can MN take?
solution: Since the circles intersect, $r_1 - r_2 < MN < r_1 + r_2$.
The whole numbers strictly between {=lo} and {=hi} are {=lo+1} to {=hi-1}, which is {=n} values.
notes: Count of integers strictly between r1-r2 and r1+r2 = 2*r2-1 (excludes touching cases). r1 >= r2+2 so lower bound >= 2.
